etymologies.etymologyHTML:
From Middle English thing, from Old English þing, from Proto-West Germanic *þing, from Proto-Germanic *þingą.

Cognate with Saterland Frisian Ding (“thing”), West Frisian ting, ding (“thing”), Dutch ding (“thing”), German Low German Ding (“thing”), German Ding (“thing”), Swedish, Danish and Norwegian ting (“thing”), Faroese ting (“parliament, assembly”), Icelandic þing (“congress, assembly”).

The word originally meant "assembly", then came to mean a specific issue discussed at such an assembly, and ultimately came to mean most broadly "an object". Compare Latin rēs, also meaning "legal matter", and same transition from Latin causa (“legal matter”) to "thing" in Romance languages. Modern use to refer to a Germanic assembly is likely influenced by cognates (from the same Proto-Germanic root) like Old Norse þing (“thing”), Danish ting, Swedish ting, and Old High German ding with this meaning.

definitions.definition: That which is considered to exist as a separate entity, object, quality or concept.

quote.citation: 1611, The Holy Bible, […] (King James Version), London:  […]  Robert Barker, […], →OCLC, Luke 1:1:
quote.text: Forasmuch as many have taken in hand to set forth in order a declaration of those things which are most surely believed among us...

quote.citation: 2013 June 21, Oliver Burkeman, “The tao of tech”, in The Guardian Weekly, volume 189, number 2, page 48:
quote.text: The dirty secret of the internet is that all this distraction and interruption is immensely profitable. Web companies like to boast about […], or offering services that let you […], "share the things you love with the world" and so on. But the real way to build a successful online business is to be better than your rivals at undermining people's control of their own attention.

definitions.definition: A word, symbol, sign, or other referent that can be used to refer to any entity.
An individual object or distinct entity.
Whatever can be owned.
Corporeal object.
(law)
(in the plural) Possessions or equipment; stuff; gear.
(somewhat dated, with the) The latest fad or fashion.

quote.citation: 1802, Anne Ormsby, "Memoirs of a Family in Swisserland", quoted in The Monthly Review, Or, Literary Journal page 45:
quote.text: To go to bed late, to rise late, to breakfast late, to dine late, and to visit late, is  to be “quite the thing,” or in good English, which you may understand better than the first phrase, to be in the fashion.

quote.citation: 2002, Roger Nichols, The Harlequin Years: Music in Paris 1917-1929, Univ of California Press, →ISBN:
quote.text: After a slow start it became the thing to do; 'everyone went to see Pbi-Pbi, no one  talked of anything but Pbi-Pbi […] '

definitions.definition: (informal) A custom or practice.
(informal) A genuine concept, entity or phenomenon; something that actually exists (often contrary to expectation or belief). [from 20th c.]

quote.citation: 1993 November 24, The Rush Limbaugh Show (radio), Rush Limbaugh (actor):
quote.text: Now I don't know how many of those male flight attendants are male lesbians -- you know... (Laughter) Well, it's a thing. I mean, there's a -- it's a -- there's a feminist professor down in Tampa who's discovered a male lesbianAccessed via COCA

quote.citation: 2014, Marianna Papastephanou, Torill Strand, Anne Pirrie, Philosophy as a Lived Experience:
quote.text: Frequent statements of the kind “'Race' is not a thing”, “'races,' put simply, do not exist”, “'race' (as each essay subtly shows) simply does not exist” aim to discredit Todorov's claim that a relapse to an ontology of race is at place  […]

quote.citation: 2014, Harper Lin, Croissant Murder:
quote.text: Clémence would say that his style was normcore before normcore became a thing. She had to admit that she still found him attractive.

quote.citation: 2019, Adam Gopnik, A Thousand Small Sanities, Riverrun, published 2019, page 88:
quote.text: Conservative philosophy, in other words, is, as we say now, a thing and deserves a serious listen.

definitions.definition: (informal) A unit or container, usually containing consumable goods.

quote.citation: 1998 March 24, Geraldo (television):
quote.text: And he invited us all in there and then he kicked the girls out a little bit later and brought me in a couple things of alcohol. And just before he brought in my second bottle of alcohol […]Accessed via COCA

quote.citation: 2011, 1:19:48 from the start, in We Were Here:
quote.text: I remember my friend Ben saying in the old days that he would never go to Costco and buy one of those big things of toilet paper […]Accessed via COCA

quote.citation: 2011, Juliette Fay, Deep Down True: A Novel, Penguin, →ISBN:
quote.text: I came home and ate a whole thing of ice cream.

definitions.definition: (informal) A problem, dilemma, or complicating factor.
(informal, with the) The central point; the crux.

That's the thing: we don't know where he is.

definitions.definition: (slang) A penis.

quote.citation: 1962 [1959], William S. Burroughs, Naked Lunch, New York: Grove Press, page 150:
quote.text: “Oh Gertie it’s true. It’s all true. They’ve got a horrid gash instead of a thrilling thing.”

definitions.definition: A living being or creature.
Used after a noun to refer dismissively to the situation surrounding the noun's referent.

quote.citation: 1914, Eugene Gladstone O'Neill, The Movie Man [playscript]:
quote.text: Don’t forget to have Gomez postpone that shooting thing. (in reference to the execution of Fernandez)

definitions.definition: (informal, used possessively) That which is favoured; personal preference.

quote.citation: 2002, Joss Whedon et al, "Never Leave Me", Buffy the Vampire Slayer (TV episode):
quote.text: Tool talk [is] not my thing.

quote.citation: 2006, Corbin Bleu, interview with Tigerbeat magazine:
quote.text: The Internet isn't my thing. I so much rather talk on the phone.

definitions.definition: (informal, used possessively, with "do") One's typical routine, habits, or manner.

quote.citation: 2006, David Lynch, Catching the Big Fish, Tarcher 2006, "Darkness", p. 91:
quote.text: But I'm just a guy from Missoula, Montana, doing my thing, going down the road like everybody else.

definitions.definition: (chiefly historical) A public assembly or judicial council in a Germanic country.

quote.citation: 1974, Jón Jóhannesson, translated by Haraldur Bessason, A History of the Old Icelandic Commonwealth: Íslendinga Saga, page 46:
quote.text: In accordance with Old Germanic custom men came to the thing fully armed, [...]

quote.citation: 1974, Jakob Benediktsson, Landnám og upphaf allsherjarríkis, in Saga Íslands, quoted in 1988 by Jesse L. Byock in Medieval Iceland: Society, Sagas, and Power, page 85:
quote.text: The goðar seem both to have received payment of thing-fararkaup from those who stayed home and at the same time compensated those who went to the thing, and it cannot be seen whether they had any profit from these transactions.

quote.citation: 1988, Jesse L. Byock, Medieval Iceland: Society, Sagas, and Power, page 59:
quote.text: All Icelandic things were skap-thing, meaning that they were governed by established procedure and met at regular legally designated intevals at predetermined meeting places.

definitions.definition: (informal) A romantic relationship.

quote.citation: 2020, David Gomadza, EVELINA: The Alpha:
quote.text: I can screw you in front of everyone. I don't care, we have a thing going on, you know. I love you,” she said.

definitions.definition: (informal) A romantic couple.
(MLE) Alternative form of ting.
(MLE) Girl; attractive woman.
(rare) To express as a thing; to reify.
